Because the math doesn't work any other way. Think of it this way, if you have 2 groups of 10 and combine them that would be 20 people. Ok, but you could just as easily write it as (2x10+5) and left to right works just fine. The only reason I can think to give the order of operations is this; there's extra work to be done somewhere in order to make sure the math is done in the right order. If we did it left to right, then that work is done while writing the math, which could make solving long problems difficult. With the order of operations, the extra work is done after is written down, so you're not doing 2 things at once.

The reason it is written as such is because the group of 5 joined one of the others before the 2 groups merged. If you wanted to get technical you would write it 5+10+10=25 since multiplication is just used to simplify numbers when you get larger addition equations. I only used the small numbers so it would be easy to see.
